name: a small garden bed seen from above: a thick weathered plank frame (lit top edge, dark underside, plank-end joints, overlapping broken corners) around four tilled soil ridges in three tones, wider-spaced bean plants on stakes with lit leaves and a few missing plants

surfaces.part: plank frame and tilled soil bed (seen from above)

answer.evidence: The bed spans rows 16-47. It is drawn straight down: the soil ridges and the plank frame fill almost the whole area. The top plank band (rows 16-17) and the bottom plank band (rows 45-46) have about the same height, so there is no foreshortened front. The only 'front' is a dark underside line at rows 46-47, which is 1-2 rows, below the 3-row minimum for a front face. There are no legs, no eave and no side face. The plants are decor on the soil. The result matches the 'top-down slab (no front)' reference.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate has 5 visible tones per tile, between the grass reference (3) and the paving reference (7). Near-flat coverage is 0%, the same as both references, so no 5x5 area is a flat fill. The measured near-neutral share of dark edge pixels is 0%, meaning the dark edges carry a tint. By eye they read as dark brown beside the wood and soil rather than a black sticker line. The frame has a lit top edge, a dark underside and plank joints. The soil ridges are mottled in three tones and the bean leaves carry highlights. The weak point is the shallow ramps: about 4 steps per material and only 17 distinct colours overall, against the 5-6 steps Beodeul uses. The surrounding dirt is also fairly uniform, with sparse grain. That keeps it slightly below the references, but the fine variation, tinted edges and absence of flat fills are in line with the same kind of ground tile.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate has no flat fills: 0% near-flat coverage, and every 5x5 block shows soil grain, plank grain or leaf dots. Its 5 visible tones per tile is above the grass reference (3) and a little below the paving reference (7). The edge pixels are 0% near-neutral, so the dark lines lean brown beside the wood and soil and green beside the leaves, which is the dark material tone Beodeul uses. The plank frame has a lit top edge, a darker underside and plank-end joints. The soil shows three ridge tones. The bean leaves are clustered with lit highlights. Weaknesses: only 17 colours in total, so each material ramp is about 3-4 steps against Beodeul's 5-6, and the leaves are small clumps of 2-3 greens. That is slightly lower than the best Beodeul pieces, but on the measured facts it is not behind the references and does not look like a sticker next to them.
